scene.speaker: freya
scene.bubble: Pet day at school! Dogs, cats, one rabbit… and Pip, the only puffin in the whole school!
scene.intro: Pet day at school! Freya has got a little brown rabbit with very long ears. Astrid has got two orange fish in a glass bowl. Have you got a dog? Have you got a cat? Everybody shows their pet — and then everybody looks at Pip, the only puffin in the class, sitting on the teacher's table like a king. Have YOU got a pet? Tell us its name!

words.clue: It says woof and loves you.
It says meow and sleeps a lot.
It swims in a little glass house.
It has long ears and hops.
It sings in its cage or in the tree.

activities.title: Match the pet with what it needs.
Listen to pet day. Write a word or number in each gap.

data.voice_note: Voces: Freya y Astrid (en el día de mascotas).
data.script: Freya: Pet day! Look, four dogs and two cats! … Astrid: Marco's rabbit is white with one grey ear. … Freya: Ana's fish is orange. His name is Sol. … Astrid: Have you got a pet, Freya? … Freya: Yes! Pip! He's a puffin. The only one in school! … Astrid: My pet is a little brown mouse. Her name is Nuez. … Freya: All the pets get a star sticker today! … Astrid: Even the fish. On his glass, of course!

activities.title: Quick check · Choose the correct word.

data.text: Ask your partner: "Have you got a pet? What is it? What's its name?" If they haven't, ask: "What pet do you want?"

activities.title: Two pictures, many differences!
activities.instructions: Look at picture A and picture B. Find the 11 differences and tell your partner about them.

homework.prompt: Draw your pet (or your dream pet) and write 3 sentences: name, colour, what it can do.

outcomes.puede: Understand short simple dialogues about family, school, animals, food (Cambridge Starters Listening parts 1–4).
Answer picture-prompted questions; describe a picture in simple sentences.
Read 2–3-sentence texts; match pictures to words and short captions.
Copy words and complete short sentences (Starters Reading/Writing parts).
~450 words (Starters wordlist); Present simple, present continuous (limited), there is/are, like + -ing.
